subtitle: Current leaders and their ties abroad

fact: Netanyahu lived in Cheltenham Township outside Philadelphia in 1956–58 and 1963–67 and graduated from Cheltenham High School in 1967.

clue: Slept in a Star Trek-themed bedroom in Iowa while learning about farming
fact: In 1985 Xi, then a county official in Hebei, led a five-man agricultural delegation to Iowa and stayed in Muscatine in the Dvorchak family's son's Star Trek-themed room.
original_clue: Slept in a Star Trek-themed bedroom in Iowa when he studied agriculture there

fact: King since 2016, he spent most of his time in Bavaria (a villa in Tutzing, the Sonnenbichl hotel in Garmisch-Partenkirchen) until protests at home in 2020, when Germany warned that Thai politics must not be conducted from German soil.
original_clue: Spends most of his time in luxury hotels and properties in Germany

clue: Worked for a US congresswoman in Washington
fact: From 1987 to 1989 Takaichi was a US congressional fellow in the office of Rep. Pat Schroeder, a Colorado Democrat.

headline: Before the History Books
subtitle: Match the leader to the strange fact
clue: Lived in Harlem and wrote about Black racial oppression
fact: The New York Times' 1969 obituary says he 'is believed to have lived in Harlem for a while' (c. 1912–13; only a New York letter survives). In 1924 he wrote essays on lynching and 'the Black race'.

clue: Wrote children's poetry before committing genocide
fact: Karadžić, a psychiatrist and poet, published the children's poems 'Ima čuda – nema čuda' (1984). The UN tribunal (ICTY) convicted him in 2016 of genocide at Srebrenica (1995); on appeal in 2019 his sentence became life.
original_clue: Wrote children's books before committing genocide

clue: Worked in French factories, including Renault, from 16 to 21
fact: Deng reached France in Oct 1920 aged 16 and left for Moscow in Jan 1926 aged 21. He worked at the Schneider steelworks in Le Creusot, a Hutchinson rubber plant and as a fitter at Renault in Billancourt.
original_clue: Worked at a car-making factory in France from when he was 16 to 21

clue: Took dance and violin lessons in London to fit in
fact: As a law student in London (1888–91) Gandhi bought a top hat and a Bond Street suit and took dancing, violin and elocution lessons to become an 'English gentleman', then quit after about three months.
source_name: Gandhi, The Story of My Experiments with Truth

clue: Avoided meat and alcohol, partly to ease chronic gas
fact: Hitler had lifelong cramps and flatulence and went meat-free in the late 1930s; his motives are debated, he did eat meat and drink beer or wine at times, and his doctors noted the diet made the gas worse.
original_clue: Never drank or ate meat, but mostly because it gave him bad farts

headline: Of Age
subtitle: The general age of consent
clue: 14 (16 with a teacher or guardian)
fact: Italy's Penal Code (art. 609-quater) sets 14, rising to 16 when the older partner is a parent, guardian, teacher or anyone else the minor is entrusted to.
source_name: Wikipedia: Age of consent by country (Italian Penal Code art. 609-quater)

clue: 16 in some regions
fact: Each state sets its own age: 16 in most states, 17 or 18 in the rest (US HHS guide to state laws).
source_name: US HHS (ASPE): Statutory Grape, A Guide to State Laws

clue: 18 under every local law (16 nationally)
fact: Nationally 16 since 2023 (13 before). All 47 prefectures also ban 'lewd' acts with under-18s; Nagano was the last to pass one, in 2016. Courts read these narrowly (exploitative sex, not every relationship).
Slovenia's Criminal Code sets the age of consent at 15, the same for everyone.
source_name: Wikipedia: Age of consent by country

clue: 21 unless married
fact: Bahrain's Penal Code (art. 345) punishes consensual sex with a female under 21; within marriage the age is 16.
source_name: Penal Code of Bahrain (1976, as amended), via UNODC

clue: 14 (21 if same-sex)
fact: Madagascar's Penal Code (art. 331) sets 14, but makes an 'indecent or unnatural act' with a same-sex partner under 21 a crime.
source_name: Wikipedia: Age of consent by country (Madagascar Penal Code of 1972, art. 331)

headline: Hard Line
subtitle: Penalties in law for graping a child
clue: 5–20 years
fact: Penal Code art. 177 (revised 2023): non-consensual intercourse, which includes any intercourse with a child under 16 (13-15 if the adult is 5+ years older), carries a fixed term of at least 5 years; art. 12 caps fixed terms at 20.
source_name: e-Gov: Penal Code (Act No. 45 of 1907), art. 177
note: Penalties written in law, not the sentences courts actually give.

clue: 20+ years to death
fact: POCSO Act as amended in 2019: penetrative sexual assault on a child under 16 is at least 20 years up to life (s.4(2)); aggravated cases, e.g. a child under 12, are at least 20 years, life for the rest of natural life, or death (s.6).

clue: Death or life in prison
fact: Penal Code s.376(3) (added 2016): grape of a minor is punished with death or imprisonment for life, plus a fine. A 2021 bill's chemical-castration clause was dropped before it passed.

clue: Up to 15 years or a fine (child under 12)
fact: Criminal Code art. 250 (Sexual Offences Act, in force 1 July 2024): penetration of a child under 12 carries up to 15 years or a fifth-category fine, with no statutory minimum; ages 12-15 are up to 12 years (art. 248).

clue: 1–5 years (no force)
fact: Criminal Code art. 187 (revised 1 July 2024): a sexual act with a child under 12 is 1 to 5 years; under 16, up to 5 years or a monetary penalty. If force or coercion is used, grape (art. 190) is 1 to 10 years.

headline: What Matters Most
subtitle: Where people found meaning in life (Pew 2021)
clue: This country mentioned hobbies more than any other surveyed
fact: Around one-in-five (22%) in the UK mentioned hobbies — the highest share of the 17 publics, and the third most-cited source there after family and friends.
source_name: Pew Research Center: What Makes Life Meaningful? (Spring 2021 Global Attitudes)

clue: This country ranked material well-being as its top source of meaning
fact: In South Korea, material well-being emerged as the top source of meaning (ahead of health and family), even though fewer people mention multiple topics than in many other publics.
source_name: Pew Research Center: What Makes Life Meaningful? (Spring 2021 Global Attitudes)

clue: This country ranked society as its top source of meaning
fact: In Taiwan, society / places / institutions was the top source of meaning (38%), above family, occupation and material well-being — unique among the 17 publics.
source_name: Pew Research Center: What Makes Life Meaningful? (Spring 2021 Global Attitudes)

clue: This country ranked health as its top source of meaning
fact: In Spain, 48% mentioned health — the top source of meaning for Spaniards, and the highest health share across the 17 publics.
source_name: Pew Research Center: What Makes Life Meaningful? (Spring 2021 Global Attitudes)

clue: This country mentioned occupation more than any other surveyed
fact: Italy had the highest occupation/career mention rate at 43%, tying family as a top source there; South Korea was lowest at 6%.
source_name: Pew Research Center: What Makes Life Meaningful? (Spring 2021 Global Attitudes)
